messages:
ashley: heads-up — ap-south1 is spiking GPU attach failures. Logs show `nvme metadata checksum mismatch` on ephemeral devices starting ~01:10 UTC. Autoscaler is seeing attach timeouts :eyes:

devin: yep, noticed several host boot loops this morning. janitor started a scrub run automatically. grabbing a sample of the node logs now.

ashley: paste of the autoscaler error: ```ERROR autoscaler: attach failed id=ap-south1-node-472 err='nvme: metadata checksum mismatch' duration=37s```

storage-bot: 12 nodes flagged degraded, 34 drives exceeded checksum error threshold. Affected pool: ap-south1-ephemeral-a.

maya: mitigation idea — slow down the scrub cadence so janitor doesn't hammer the I/O. If we do that we won't reclaim as quickly which will block some GPU attachments. Tradeoff: immediate attach success vs longer reclaim window.

jordan_oncall: can we correlate with last-night's kernel nvme patch? We shipped kernel build 2023.11.7-nvme at 00:40 UTC.

rick: kernel revert would need rolling reboots across the region. That could kill ~1000 GPU-hours while we validate. Also ops-cost: provisioning stalls -> more fallback to dedicated, higher spend.

ops-qa: short-term routing: can we shift new large batch jobs out of ap-south1 to eu-west2/us-east1? Small latency-sensitive requests can stay but avoid GPU-hungry launches.

devin: quick diagnostic snippet I ran on an affected host: ```# sudo smartctl -a /dev/nvme0n1 | grep -i checksum
SMART overall-health self-assessment test result: FAILED
Error Count: 13
Firmware Rev: 3.4.1
nvme admin cmd: metadata checksum mismatch at lba 0x1f4a```

maya: suggested interim janitor config to reduce scrub pressure: ```janitor:
  scrub_parallelism: 2
  scrub_rate_limit_mb_s: 20
  verify_mode: read_only_only
```

ashley: decision so far: 1) throttle janitor as in maya's config; 2) mark ap-south1-ephemeral-a as constrained for large job placement; 3) spin up +150 GPUs from our dedicated pool in us-east for 6 hours to cover critical workloads.

devin: note on implications — throttling scrub will increase the time-to-detect true badblocks, possible longer-term wear. We should tag this as a monitored experiment.

jordan_oncall: I'll kick off a 3-node canary to revert kernel nvme patch and run GPU attach tests. If canary is green -> schedule broader rollback in a 30m window.

storage-bot: snapshot of metrics at 01:30 UTC: {degraded_nodes:12, gpu_attach_failures_last_30m:182, scrub_iops_peak:+65%}.

rick: cost note — dedicated capacity bump estimated cost ~$4.2k/hr for 150 GPUs on demand. We can trim to 100 if budget is tight.

ashley: opened vendor support ticket referencing firmware 3.4.1 and kernel build. Also filing incident doc. Will post updates.

ops-qa: routing change applied to scheduler: large job placements avoid ap-south1 for 3 hours. Monitoring alert created for gpu_attach_fail > 50.

janitor-bot: janitor config updated (throttled) by maya. New scrub rate 20MB/s, parallelism 2.

devin: temporary checklist before broad revert: gather core dumps, nvme ctrl logs, ensure device firmware baseline, snapshot affected blockmaps.

ashley: thanks team. priority: stabilize attaches without mass reboots. we'll reconvene in 20m with canary results. :thumbsup:
